statements.text: The Prime Minister told the Commons he raised an energy ceasefire with President Trump in New York. He said an energy ceasefire, with both sides stopping their attacks, is the quickest way to get diesel back onto world markets without rewarding the aggressor. He welcomed President Trump's announcement of a reciprocal energy ceasefire, and said President Zelenskyy has assured him Ukraine would implement it immediately once a start date is confirmed.

The Prime Minister has asked Ministers to draw up further sanctions, military support and fiscal packages to provide urgent support in the coming weeks, and is set to tell President Zelenskyy that the UK will accelerate delivery of critical air defence missiles.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said UK support for Ukraine is vital for keeping the UK safe, that the UK is with Ukraine for as long as it takes and will go further and faster, and that Russia's aggression cannot be allowed to succeed on the continent.

The UK will accelerate deliveries of British Lightweight Multirole Missiles, which have proven extremely effective against jet-powered drones. The UK has committed £1.6 billion to deliver more than 5000 to Ukraine over four years, and will accelerate £10 million of a £45 million missile package to meet Ukraine's most urgent winter needs. At the 14 October meeting the Prime Minister set out the latest LMM package, and the leaders discussed how the UK could accelerate defensive support ahead of winter, including on long range missiles.

The Prime Minister welcomed President Zelenskyy to Downing Street on 14 October. The leaders reflected on Russia's indiscriminate attacks on civilians and energy infrastructure since President Trump called for an energy ceasefire, and agreed Russia had no interest in peace. The Prime Minister said the UK would continue to develop innovative military solutions, including retrofitting British capability onto equipment gifted by other partners, and would continue its diplomatic efforts to support international supplies of defensive equipment.

speakers: Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey
statements.text: Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey urged partners to back the ban on Russian LNG, like the UK, to curtail the war chest funding Putin, and is to urge partners at the IMF meetings in Bangkok to fully implement an equivalent ban. The Foreign Secretary did the same with partners at the Warsaw Security Forum.

A UK government spokesperson said Ukraine has repeatedly shown it is serious about peace, while Russia has repeatedly rejected full and partial ceasefires and continues attacks on Ukrainian civilians and energy, and that Russia could end the war today.

The Prime Minister said the UK has recently announced new funding to help Ukraine get through its fifth winter under Russian bombardment, and a new sanctions package that brings over 90% of Russia's oil producing capacity under UK sanctions.

The Prime Minister said the UK's assessment is that the incident at RAF Fairford is highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran and almost certainly directed by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard. He said the UK will not tolerate these threats, will crack down on Iran's use of criminal networks, and will bring further sanctions to restrict the capacity of Iran and the IRGC to harm the UK.

The Prime Minister said Russia is conducting a campaign of hybrid attacks and sabotage across Europe. He said he and Chancellor Merz agreed a new partnership in Berlin to tackle these threats, and confirmed the commitment to establish a National Centre for Information Defence, as recommended by the Foreign Affairs Select Committee.

The Prime Minister confirmed Britain's decision to send air defence and a Voyager aircraft to Saudi Arabia for air-to-air refuelling, said a Voyager has already completed 14 operational missions, condemned the attacks on King Khalid International Airport, and said the UK will continue to stand with Saudi Arabia against the Houthis.

The UK-EU summit will take place in Brussels on 20 November. On the table are a food and drink trade deal, progress on emissions trading and linking energy systems, a youth experience scheme and deeper immigration cooperation. A food and drink deal is expected to add over £10 billion a year to the UK economy by 2040. The Prime Minister said he will work hard over the next five weeks to secure a deal.

The Prime Minister said being open to discussing the UK's relationship with the EU in the longer term would enhance the chances of a successful summit outcome. He said that after the summit a serious dialogue on the options for the long-term relationship should be set up, and that the British public will be the boss at every stage.

On 15 October the Prime Minister invited the First Minister to work with him to push more power out of Westminster and Holyrood, and to develop with the UK Government through No10 North and the Scotland Office a new model of regional empowerment. Andy Burnham said he was making an offer to the Scottish Government. Douglas Alexander said the offer is a genuine one, and the Scotland Office is ready to work alongside the Scottish Government to make it happen.

In his 16 October speech in Motherwell the Prime Minister made what he called a serious and genuine offer to the Scottish Government to design a new model of regional economic empowerment across Scotland. The offer includes DWP devolution, a localised employment support model shaped by Holyrood, and a meeting of the National Economic Council with the First Ministers of Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland in a couple of weeks.

The Prime Minister said to John Swinney that he wants to push economic power out into Scotland's regions, asked whether Swinney does too, and proposed agreeing a new process and proposal with Douglas Alexander and Swinney's team, with both governments working together towards a joint ambition.

The Prime Minister said the Scottish Government has this week agreed to match the UK government's £10 million to create two defence technical excellence colleges, one in the east and one in the west, and credited Douglas Alexander and John Swinney for working together on it.

The Prime Minister said around one in six young people in Scotland are not in education, employment or training. He said the review led by Alan Milburn is challenging the government to build a system on the Easterhouse principle of names not numbers, built from the bottom up.

The Prime Minister said he wants a change in public procurement across the UK, working with the devolved governments, to back a plan to reindustrialise Britain. He cited Greater Manchester buses that he said were built by Alexander Dennis in Falkirk.
The Prime Minister said the UK takes the G20 presidency in 2027, with AI centre stage, and that the aim during the presidency year is to agree a single set of global principles and standards on AI.

Great British Railways' headquarters is to be built at Becketwell, a brownfield site in Derby city centre, for up to 450 GBR staff. Construction is expected to begin in early 2027 and be completed by spring 2029, and the HQ is expected to bring hundreds of rail jobs and an estimated £151 million boost to Derby's economy. Heidi Alexander said she is delighted Becketwell will become GBR's new home.

Up to 600 apprentices aged 16 to 21 will enrol over the next four years on the rail foundation apprenticeship, with the first starters based in Derby. Pat McFadden said this is part of a £2.5 billion youth employment support package creating up to 500,000 opportunities. Claire Ward said she is particularly pleased about the 600 apprenticeship places.
The King has appointed William James Baxter QPM DL as Lord-Lieutenant of County Tyrone, succeeding Sir Robert William Lowry Scott, who retired on 17 June 2026.
